claim: JWT dates are NumericDate values: the number of seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z UTC, ignoring leap seconds.
quote: A JSON numeric value representing the number of seconds from 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z UTC until the specified UTC date/time, ignoring leap seconds.

claim: If a validator does not find itself in a token's audience list, it has to reject the token.
quote: If the principal processing the claim does not identify itself with a value in the "aud" claim when this claim is present, then the JWT MUST be rejected.

claim: When a JWT's signature fails to validate, the recipient has to report the failure back to the issuer.
quote: If the signature on the JWT cannot be validated, the recipient MUST notify the issuer that the JWT was rejected.

claim: Validators may allow a few minutes of leeway when checking a token's expiration time, to account for clock skew.
quote: Implementers MAY provide for some small leeway, usually no more than a few minutes, to account for clock skew.

claim: Every JWT must include an expiration time; a token without "exp" is not valid.
quote: The "exp" (expiration time) claim identifies the expiration time on or after which the JWT MUST NOT be accepted for processing.

claim: A JWT that carries personal data must be encrypted as a JWE rather than only signed.
quote: If the JOSE Header is for a JWE, the JWT is represented as a JWE and the claims are encrypted, with the JWT Claims Set being the plaintext encrypted by the JWE.

claim: The "iat" claim requires validators to reject tokens whose issue time is in the future.
A JWT parser must either reject a token with duplicate claim names or keep only the last occurrence of each duplicated name.
quote: The Claim Names within a JWT Claims Set MUST be unique; JWT parsers MUST either reject JWTs with duplicate Claim Names or use a JSON parser that returns only the lexically last duplicate member name, as specified in Section 15.12 ("The JSON Object") of ECMAScript 5.1 [ECMAScript].
